title: Analysis of cellulose synthase activity in Arabidopsis using spinning disk microscopy
protocol: Prepare the metal slide for imaging.
Apply vacuum grease in two thin lines on each side of the round opening of the metal slide.
Place a rectangular coverslip above the opening and press firmly to the metal slide on the sides.
Flip over the metal slide.
Add a small amount of water or media to the coverslip.
Transfer one to three etiolated seedlings carefully to the water/media droplets and place them in the middle of the coverslip.
Melt 0.8% agarose for preparation of an agarose pad.
Place melted agarose on a round coverslip.
Carefully place a second round coverslip on top of the agarose.
Store prepared agarose pads in a petri dish on parafilm.
Remove the upper round coverslip from the agarose pad.
Carefully place the agarose pad with attached round coverslip on top of the seedlings at an angle to avoid air bubbles.
Absorb excess water/media by cautiously placing a corner of a tissue close to the agarose pad edge.
The prepared sample is ready for imaging.
Add a thin layer of immersion oil to the 100x objective.
Place the metal slide with the prepared sample on top, ensuring the rectangular coverslip touches the oil.
Attach a 22x32 mm coverslip to one side of the metal slide using silicone vacuum grease applied to each side of the opening.
Press the coverslip firmly onto the slide without touching the center area.
Flip the metal slide over so that the coverslip is below it, and place it on a stand with the coverslip not touching any surface.
Mount an etiolated seedling onto the prepared metal slide and coverslip.
Add approximately 10 μL of sterile water or sterile liquid ½ MS medium to the center of the coverslip without touching the glass.
Carefully lift an etiolated seedling from the plate using a toothpick or fine forceps and transfer it to the coverslip.
Place one to three hypocotyls centered in the middle of the slide.
Cover the etiolated seedling with an agarose pad.
Separate the upper coverslip from the lower one, leaving the agarose pad attached to one of the round coverslips.
Discard the round coverslip without the agarose.
Carefully place the agarose and coverslip, agarose side down, on top of the seedlings.
Absorb excess water or media with a tissue to reduce seedling drift during imaging.
Be very careful not to disturb the seedling during mounting.
Image etiolated hypocotyl epidermal cells using an inverted spinning disk confocal microscope equipped with a sCMOS camera and a 100 × oil-immersion objective.
Use excitation wavelengths of 488 nm for GFP, 515 nm for YFP, or 561 nm for RFP/tdTomato depending on the fluorophore attached to the CESA protein.
Apply band emission filters: 525/36 nm for GFP, 540/24 nm for YFP, and 605/52 nm for RFP/tdTomato.
Place a drop of immersion oil on the objective lens.
Transfer the slide with the rectangular coverslip facing the microscope objective.
Use low laser power (∼15% of 60 mW) to prevent photo-bleaching.
Set exposure times between 100–200 ms for imaging.
Locate cells approximately two cells below the apical hook.
Move to the plasma membrane focal plane where there are active CSCs.
Identify the plasma membrane focal plane by moving towards the cell surface.
Avoid stressed or dead cells and cells with no fluorescent signal.
Activate the focus maintenance system for Nikon microscopes.
Re-adjust the focus if necessary after activating the focus maintenance system.
Take a 10-min movie with 10 s time intervals.
Set the exposure time to 300–800 ms depending on the fluorescent marker.
Go to ‘Plugins -> StackReg’ and select the ‘Rigid Body’ transformation.
Correct for XY-drift using the selected Rigid Body transformation.
Use the preinstalled Fiji plugin under ‘Plugins -> Registration -> Rigid Registration’ as an alternative.
Reduce background noise by selecting ‘Analyze -> Multi Kymograph -> Walking Average’ (3 frame average).
Select ‘Process -> Enhance contrast…’ to enhance signal intensity.
Set the saturated pixels value to around 0.4%.
Select ‘Process all X slices’ to process all images in the stack.
Use ‘Process -> Subtract Background’ for background subtraction.
Set a rolling ball radius of ∼50 px for background subtraction.
Optimize laser power and exposure times during live-cell imaging.
Save adjusted image stacks in TIFF format.
Process all images identically for consistency.
